name: Depth Anything 3
plain: ByteDance's Depth Anything 3: depth from one image, with relative, metric and multi-view versions. The licence differs by variant, see the table.
summary: Depth Anything 3 (Lin et al. 2025, ByteDance): monocular depth from a DINOv2 ViT with DPT heads; relative (Mono), metric (Metric), any-view depth with camera (Large, Giant) and Giant aligned to Metric (Nested).

papers.title: Depth Anything 3: Recovering the Visual Space from Any Views

licence_notes: The Mono and Metric weights are Apache-2.0 but their training data terms are unchecked (a note only); the other variants' weights are CC-BY-NC-4.0 (`no`).
task_io: Input: one RGB image. Output: a depth or inverse-depth map. `kind` (a card field, `result.kind`) says what the numbers mean: `metric` = metres; `scale_invariant`, `affine_invariant` and `affine_invariant_inverse` are relative (unknown scale or shift, not metres). Metric models that use the focal length take `model(image, intrinsics=K)` (K `[3, 3]`, pixels of the input): `metric3d-vit-large` and `da3metric-large` need it for correct metres (`da3metric-large`: metres = output x focal / 300; without `intrinsics=` a 300 px focal length is assumed, wrong for a real camera). `unidepth-v2-vitl14`, `unik3d-vitl`, `depth-pro` and MoGe estimate the camera themselves (given `intrinsics=` replace `fx`); `zoedepth-nk` and the relative models (`da3mono-large` too) take none.

parity.text: CPU, float32: max |diff| <= 0.005 vs the original. GPU, float16 (the default), portable and kernels: mean |diff| <= 0.5 % and p99 <= 2 % of the reference's median |value| (absolute error of the output `depth`).
